## Summary

Did 2.3 after 2.2 in the same session: the context policy. The nudge now has one home, packages/engine/src/driver/nudge.ts — dependency-free because the PostToolUse hook reads it on the 100ms hot path and must not import the spawn surface for an env var name. The adapter writes {ts, pct, tokens} to the path it hands the child in SOFAR_DRIVE_NUDGE; the hook turns that file's EXISTENCE into "finish the CURRENT task now, then hand off…", delivers it BEFORE the record is resolved and even where it cannot be (the nudge is a fact about the process, not the record), and stays silent in every session no driver started. Contents are detail: an unreadable file still nudges, without the number. Driver side: watchThreshold reads the gauge immediately and then every 2s and nudges ONCE (the file persists, so the hook re-injects by itself); a nudged session that wrote back and resolved a task hands off with reason `threshold`, not task_done. The prompt now differs by policy and that difference is load-bearing — print mode ends the turn on its own, so a threshold session is told to keep taking tasks until nudged, while a task session is told to do one. Schema: run_started gained context_window, REQUIRED for threshold exactly as threshold_pct is (D7) — 80% of 200k and 80% of 1M are two runs wearing one id, and sofar never infers the window from a model name. --resume consequently refuses to change a run's policy and takes the run's own numbers over the resuming driver's flags. Tests: 32 in drive.test.ts (5 new for threshold), 5 new hook tests, schema and driver-events fixtures updated for the new field; full suite green at 1786. Smoke-tested through the built CLI twice: the hook injects the line with the gauge, and a threshold run nudged at 85%, the child read the detail file, and the record shows `threshold 80% of 200000 — 1 handoff (1 threshold)`.
